chunks: From Al-Subah ibn Siyabah, he said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'Is the affliction that befalls a believer due to a sin?' He said: 'No, but so that He may hear his wailing, his complaint, and his supplication, for which good deeds are recorded for him, misdeeds are wiped out from him, and a treasure is amassed for him on the Day of Resurrection.'
ai.seo_question: Why do believers face afflictions if not as punishment for sins?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that afflictions befalling believers are not necessarily punishment for sins, but rather a means for Allah to hear their supplications and complaints. These trials serve to record good deeds, expiate sins, and accumulate a spiritual treasure for the Day of Resurrection.

en.muhajir-b-ali: I asked Abu 'Abd Allah (a.s), 'The affliction that befalls a believer is it because of a sin?' 'No,' he replied, 'It is so that He (Allah) may hear his wails and complaints and supplications for which good deeds are recorded for him and misdeeds are wiped out from him, and a treasure is amassed for him for the Day of Resurrection.
